x_posts.text: Mirra Andreeva beat Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 at the WTA Finals. She came back from 1-4 down in set 1, then bageled the No. 2 seed. 11 consecutive games. 62 minutes. She's into the semis. #WTAFinals #Tennis

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: WTA Finals Day 5 today: Pegula vs Gauff — both 1-1, one spot left in Group 1. And Sabalenka vs Svitolina — both 1-1, one spot left in Group 2. Noskova and Andreeva are waiting. #WTAFinals #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
The WTA Finals has its first big storyline, and it's one almost no one expected.

Mirra Andreeva walked into Wednesday's match against Aryna Sabalenka down 1-4 in the first set. What happened next was extraordinary. She won five straight games to take the set 6-4, then bageled the world No. 2 in the second set 6-0. Eleven consecutive games. The match lasted 62 minutes. Andreeva, who is 2-0 in the round robin, is now confirmed for the semifinals.

Sabalenka falls to 1-1 and needs a win on Thursday to stay alive. In the other Group 2 match, Elina Svitolina beat Karolina Muchova in three sets to also stay alive at 1-1 — Muchova is eliminated at 0-2.

Today (Thursday, November 12) is decision day for both groups. Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula play with the second Group 1 semi spot on the line, and Sabalenka and Svitolina fight for Group 2. Only two players will join Linda Noskova and Mirra Andreeva in the semifinals.

Who do you think survives — Gauff or Pegula? And can Sabalenka recover after Wednesday's beatdown?

facebook.long_form:
The 2026 Nitto ATP Finals groups are official.

This morning in Turin, the draw ceremony placed the eight qualified players into two round-robin groups. The John McEnroe Group features year-end No. 1 Alexander Zverev, Ben Shelton, Arthur Fils, and Rafael Jodar. The Ivan Lendl Group has Carlos Alcaraz, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli, and Frances Tiafoe.

The headline storyline: Zverev and Alcaraz are in separate groups, which means — if both advance — they would only meet in the semifinals. For the first three days of the tournament (starting November 15), the two title favorites are on opposite ends of the bracket.

The other big narrative is the Lendl Group. Alcaraz and Medvedev have played in Grand Slam finals before, and their round-robin match at the Inalpi Arena will likely be the most-watched group stage match of the week.

Also worth noting: four first-time participants in Turin — Cobolli, Tiafoe, Jodar, and Fils — make this one of the most generationally diverse ATP Finals in recent memory.

Who wins the John McEnroe Group? Let us know your prediction below.

stories.title: Sabalenka's No. 2 Ranking Under Threat After Andreeva's 6-0 Dismantling

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: Aryna Sabalenka is now fighting for her WTA year-end No. 2 ranking, not just a semifinal spot. Andreeva gave her a 6-0 second set. The gap between No. 2 and No. 3 just got a lot smaller. #WTAFinals #TennisRankings

facebook.long_form:
Aryna Sabalenka entered the WTA Finals in Indian Wells as the second-best player on the planet, by ranking. Wednesday might have changed that conversation.

After losing 6-4, 6-0 to Mirra Andreeva in just 62 minutes, Sabalenka is not only fighting for a semifinal place — she is fighting to protect her year-end No. 2 ranking. Andreeva, ranked No. 3, is 2-0 and already in the semifinals. The more Andreeva advances, and the earlier Sabalenka exits, the closer the gap in the rankings becomes.

The 6-0 second set was not just a scoreline. It showed Andreeva, who has been rising all season, is now at a level where she can dominate Sabalenka on this stage. That is a significant shift from where the two players stood even six months ago.

Sabalenka plays Svitolina today. A win keeps her season alive. But the broader message from Wednesday is that the conversation around the WTA's top two is no longer settled.

What do you think — is Andreeva ready to take the No. 2 ranking this year?

facebook.long_form:
Now that the groups are set, here is what to watch when the 2026 Nitto ATP Finals begins in Turin on November 15.

The Ivan Lendl Group is the glamour draw. Carlos Alcaraz arrives with five 2026 titles, a 10-match winning streak, and the momentum of back-to-back Masters crowns in Vienna and Paris. Daniil Medvedev is a former world No. 1 who has won at the ATP Finals before. Their round-robin match has Grand Slam final energy — these two have made each other's season harder before, and Turin will be no different. Flavio Cobolli and Frances Tiafoe are both first-timers with the game to cause a surprise.

The John McEnroe Group looks more predictable on paper — but only slightly. Alexander Zverev is the year-end No. 1, a Roland Garros and US Open champion, and a two-time ATP Finals winner. If he is at his 2026 best, Shelton, Fils, and Jodar will find him very difficult to beat. But Ben Shelton reached the Paris Masters final two weeks ago, and Arthur Fils has been a consistent top-10 presence all year. Jodar, who qualified in his ATP Tour debut year — a first in the tournament's history — is a genuine wildcard.

The tournament starts November 15 and runs through November 22.

Which group-stage match are you most excited about?

stories.title: WTA Finals Day 5 — Two Decisive Matches Today Settle the Final Semifinal Spots

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: Two matches Thursday complete the WTA Finals semifinal picture. Gauff vs Pegula in Group 1. Sabalenka vs Svitolina in Group 2. Both pairs are 1-1. Both matches are elimination games. Noskova and Andreeva have their bags packed for the semis. #WTAFinals

facebook.long_form:
Thursday's WTA Finals schedule in Indian Wells is the most important day of the round-robin stage. Both groups decide their second semifinalist on the same day.

In Group 1, Coco Gauff (1-1) faces Jessica Pegula (1-1). Linda Noskova has already secured the first spot; the winner of this match takes the second. Gauff has been on a good second-half run but lost to Noskova earlier in the week. Pegula beat Kostyuk in straight sets and will be looking to keep the momentum going. Their rivalry is one of tennis's most watched — they know each other's games as well as any two players on tour.

In Group 2, Aryna Sabalenka (1-1) must bounce back from Wednesday's humbling 6-0 set against Mirra Andreeva to face Elina Svitolina (1-1). Svitolina, who beat Karolina Muchova in three sets on Wednesday, is in form. Sabalenka needs to find the level she showed in her opening win over Muchova. For both players, it is win or go home.

The WTA Finals semifinals and final run through Sunday, November 15, completing the season-ending event in Indian Wells.

Who are you rooting for to advance: Gauff or Pegula? Sabalenka or Svitolina?
